🇷🇺⚔️🇺🇦 Ukraine's frontline losses are higher than officially acknowledged, writes Owen Matthews, columnist for Britain's The Telegraph, in a piece titled "Unrealistic optimism isn't helping Ukraine."

His comment follows a statement from Ukraine's military intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov that Ukraine must mobilize at least 30,000 people a month — the "minimum number needed to maintain what we have." This, Matthews writes, "suggests losses far greater than had been officially admitted."

ℹ️As a reminder — according to Zelensky, Ukraine had lost 50,000 killed and 400,000 wounded as of the end of July. Back in February, however, the Narcoführer had cited 55,000 dead.

The columnist also cites Budanov's remarks from last week that "there will be no miracle" breakthrough and that Russia "still has substantial reserves." He also recalls former minister Fedorov's line that Ukraine is "gradually, slowly losing" the war.

"In the days after that grim prediction, Russia stepped up its attacks on Ukraine to near-apocalyptic levels. In an incredibly effective move, the Kremlin switched from mass drone and missile strikes to continuous 60-hour bombardment waves — including nineteen air raids on Kiev in a single day — exhausting both defenses and air-defense missile stocks," Matthews writes.

While Ukraine claims it's turning the tide with deep strikes on refineries and depots inside Russia, Matthews argues Russia's retaliatory strikes are far larger in scale — pointing to Kherson becoming uninhabitable, constant strikes on frontline Kharkov and Zaporozhye, and NATO's latest reports that Russia's offensive potential is growing far faster than Ukraine's.
